figures.caption: Figure 1. Supervision granularity for EEG queries with varying confidence. (a) Existing TTA methods typically assign selected queries single-image or partial-label supervision, excluding the rest. (b) HSTTA uses the gallery hierarchy to select an appropriate supervision granularity based on each query’s current confidence.

Figure 2. Overview of HSTTA. (a)(b) Ward tree H construction and threshold θ̂ calibration before adaptation. (c) Localization of each query to its finest reliable level. (d) Level-wise supervision. (e) Per-epoch LoRA updates with re-localization every t epochs.
Table 2. HSTTA component ablation on THINGS-EEG2 with SAMGA. Lloc dist is the local distribution-alignment term in Eq. (11).
Table 3. Generalization to other pretrained EEG encoders on THINGS-EEG2 under standard 200-way retrieval.

Figure 3. Reliability and sensitivity of CSCC. (a) Actual accuracy of CSCC-calibrated pseudo-labels across target α on THINGS-EEG2. (b) Top: HSTTA top-1 across α, relative to the selected α; bottom: query distribution over tree levels at epoch 0.
Figure 4. Accuracy of (a) single-image and (b) candidate-set pseudo-labels, annotated as acc. (correct/total); (c) wrong pseudolabels, annotated as wrong (supervised). Shading: s.e. over folds.
Figure 5. (a) Multi-image: a mid-level or coarse node; Excluded: no query-specific pseudo-label (the root for HSTTA). (b) Uncertain queries are those at non-leaf nodes. †: p < 0.05 vs. HSTTA.
